name: Suspension Trainer Row
summary: A bodyweight horizontal pull performed on suspension straps that targets the upper back, lats, and biceps while demanding core stability.

setup: Secure the suspension trainer to a stable overhead anchor point.
Grasp the handles with a neutral grip and face the anchor point.
Walk your feet forward to lean back into the straps until your arms are fully extended and your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
steps: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to maintain a rigid plank posture.
Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows back and retracting your shoulder blades.
Pause briefly at the top when your hands reach the sides of your ribcage.
Lower yourself back under control until your arms are fully extended without breaking alignment.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your body down, and exhale forcefully as you pull your chest to the handles.
cues: Keep a rigid plank from head to heels.
Lead with your chest, not your hips.

common_faults.fault: Sagging at the hips or hyperextending the lower back during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Squeeze the glutes and brace the abdominals to keep the hips in line with the torso.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
common_faults.correction: Depress the shoulder blades down and back before initiating the pull.

common_faults.fault: Using hip momentum or kipping to complete the repetition.
common_faults.correction: Walk the feet back to a more upright angle to reduce resistance and maintain strict control.

precautions: Ensure the anchor point and straps are securely attached before placing your body weight onto the handles.
Maintain continuous tension on the straps throughout the entire repetition.
